name: Barack Obama

lean.basis: Democratic Illinois state senator, U.S. senator and two-term Democratic president; has campaigned for Democratic candidates since leaving office.

photo.credit: Official White House Photo by Pete Souza

current_role: Former President of the United States (2009–2017); head of the Obama Foundation
summary: Barack Obama was the 44th president of the United States from 2009 to 2017, after serving as a U.S. senator from Illinois (2005–2008) and an Illinois state senator. Since leaving office he has campaigned for Democratic candidates, including Joe Biden in 2020 and Kamala Harris in 2024, and remains the party's most prominent figure.

timeline.role: Founder; leads the Obama Foundation and presidential center

connections.name: Joe Biden
connections.description: Obama chose Biden as his 2008 running mate; Biden served as his vice president for both terms, and Obama campaigned for Biden in 2020. In July 2024 Obama privately questioned whether Biden could still win.

connections.name: Hillary Clinton
connections.description: Obama beat Clinton in a close 2008 Democratic primary; she then endorsed him at the convention.

connections.name: Hillary Clinton
connections.description: Obama appointed his former primary rival as Secretary of State; she served 2009 to 2013.

sources.title: Biographies of the Secretaries of State: Hillary Rodham Clinton — Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State

connections.name: Kamala Harris
connections.description: Barack and Michelle Obama endorsed Harris for president in a video released July 26, 2024, after Biden withdrew; Obama later campaigned for her in swing states.

connections.description: Trump accused Obama of "treason" over the 2016 Russia investigation on July 22, 2025; Obama's office called the claims "bizarre" and "a weak attempt at distraction." Obama has criticized Trump's administration in speeches.

connections.name: Brian Schatz
